---
title: 'Trigger status'
sidebarTitle: 'Trigger status'
description: 'See every trigger in your project, how it has been running, and who gets alerted when it fails.'
---

The trigger status page lists every trigger in your project, whether it belongs to an agent or a workforce. Use it to spot failing triggers, see why one stopped, and set up failure alarms on many triggers at once.

## Opening the page

Click **Triggers** in the main sidebar. The page opens with the heading **Trigger status**.

<Note>
The **Triggers** entry only shows for users who can create agents and workforces in the project. If you don't see it, ask a project admin to check your role.
</Note>

## Trigger health

The **Current trigger health** card shows the share of triggers in your project that are healthy, with a line such as "2 of 40 triggers are failing right now". It reflects each trigger's status at this moment. Only failed triggers count against it, so paused triggers still count as healthy.

The **Runs per day** chart beside it covers the last 14 days. Each day's bar splits into successful runs in green and failed runs in red, and a red dot marks every day with a failure. Hover over a day to see its run counts and the names of the triggers that failed that day.

Both the card and the chart cover the whole project, so they don't change when you search or switch tabs.

## Trigger table

The table has these columns:

| Column | What it shows |
|--------|---------------|
| **Alarm** | Your failure alarm bell, with avatars of the people who get alerted |
| **Trigger** | The trigger's name and an icon for its type |
| **Belonging to** | The agent or workforce that owns the trigger. Click it to open that agent or workforce. |
| **Status** | **Failed**, **Paused**, **Cancelled** or **Active** |
| **Last successful run** | When the trigger last ran successfully |
| **Last failed** | When the trigger last failed. A failure in the last 14 days shows in red. |
| **Task volume (14d)** | How many items the trigger produced in the last 14 days, one for each event it accepted |

The table opens sorted by status, with failed triggers first. Click a column header to sort by that column. Use the search bar to find a trigger by its name or the name of its workforce or agent.

The tabs above the table change how triggers are grouped:

- **All** lists every trigger in one table.
- **By workforce** groups triggers under the workforce they start.
- **By agent** groups triggers under the agent that owns them directly.

In the grouped tabs, click a group to expand it. Each group header shows how many triggers it has and how many are failing.

## Trigger details

Click a row to open the details panel. It shows the trigger's owner, status and last runs, and its own **Runs per day** chart for the last 14 days. Click the owner and trigger name at the top to open the agent or workforce in a new tab.

For an agent's trigger, click **Edit trigger** to open it in the agent's trigger settings. This button only shows for users who can edit agents, and it isn't available for workforce triggers.

### Why a trigger was turned off

When the platform pauses a trigger, the panel says why and what to do next:

| Reason | What to do |
|--------|------------|
| Your organization ran out of credits or actions | Add credits or upgrade your plan, then turn the trigger back on |
| Your organization or project reached a credit or action limit set in its spend controls | Raise or remove the limit, then turn the trigger back on |
| The workforce no longer has the step the trigger starts | Connect the trigger to a step in the workforce again, or delete it |
| The person who set the trigger up lost access to the files it watches | Turn it back on as someone with access to those files, or delete it |
| The connected account stopped accepting our sign-in | Reconnect the account, then turn the trigger back on |
| The schedule passed its end date | Set a later end date or remove it, then turn the trigger back on |

### Who gets alerted

The **Who gets alerted when this trigger fails** section lists each alarm on the trigger, with its owner and channels. Alarms that are switched off show as **Muted**. If you don't have an alarm on the trigger yet, click **Set up alarm** here.

## Setting up an alarm on one trigger

Each person sets up their own alarm, and the bell in the **Alarm** column shows yours. It's filled in when your alarm is on.

- If your alarm is off, click the bell to open the alarm settings. Choose where to be notified (email, Slack or Teams), then click **Enable alarm**.
- If your alarm is on, click the bell to mute it straight away.

You get a message when the trigger starts failing and another when it runs again. Under **Additional configuration** you can set the **Cooldown**, which is how long to wait before notifying again (60 minutes by default), and turn off **Notify when recovered**. If you use Invent, you can also turn on **Auto-diagnose with Invent** to have Invent look into the failure and include a proposed fix with the notification.

The avatars beside the bell show who has an alarm on the trigger. Project editors see everyone. Other members see only themselves.

For more on notification channels, see [Alerts](/build/agents/build-your-agent/alerts).

## Bulk alarm actions

You can set up or mute alarms on many triggers at once.

### Selecting triggers

Check the box at the start of each row you want. The checkbox in the header selects every trigger on the current page, and Shift-click selects a range. Your selection stays as you change pages, search or switch tabs.

An action bar at the bottom of the page shows how many triggers are selected, for example "3 selected". Click the count to see the selected triggers and remove any of them. Click the **x** at the right of the bar to clear the selection.

### Setting up alarms in bulk

1. Select the triggers.
2. In the action bar, click **Set up alarm**.
3. Choose your notification channels, then click **Enable alarms**.

If you already have an alarm on some of the triggers, they get the channels you choose in place of their current ones. They keep their own cooldown and recovery setting unless you change those too. The next time you open the bulk alarm settings on the page, they start with the settings you last used.

### Muting alarms in bulk

1. Select the triggers.
2. In the action bar, click **Mute alarms**.

Muting starts as soon as you click. Only triggers where your alarm is on are muted, and the rest stay selected. If none of the selected triggers has your alarm on, the button is disabled.

### When a bulk action finishes

The action bar shows progress while it runs, for example "Enabling alarms… 3/10". When it's done, a message confirms the result, for example "Alarms enabled for 10 triggers" or "Enabled for 7 triggers, 3 failed".

- Triggers that succeeded leave your selection.
- Triggers you can't change, because you don't have permission or alarms aren't available for that trigger type, are named in the message and leave your selection.
- Triggers that failed for any other reason stay selected, so you can try again.
